title: Investigation of the Valence Band Edge of ONO Cells in Flash Memory Using Z-contrast Imaging
content: NAND flash memory is a state-of-the-art device that has been increasingly used due to high data storage density and low power consumption [1]. The physics of NAND operation involves Fowler–Nordheim tunneling of charge carriers through a dielectric layer when a gate voltage is applied to the memory cell [2]. In charge-trap nitride (CTN) storage-based flash memory, electrons or holes are injected into the CTN layer via the silicon oxynitride (SiON) tunneling layer during program or erase cycles. One of the most efficient ways to improve the device performance of NAND flash memory cells is by bandgap engineering of the SiON layer [3], [4]. For example, precise control of the N concentration in the SiON tunneling layer reduces the energy bandgap of the electronic structure, thereby boosting the erasure speed [5].
